lesson_title: Same Sun, Same Air, Totally Different Life
hook_text: Two places in South Africa get the same sunshine and the same air. One is a jungle. One is nearly empty. Why?
clip_script: Every living thing carries a survival backpack with five things in it. Energy, almost always from the Sun, captured by plants. Gases: oxygen to release energy, carbon dioxide for plants to make food. Water: you are sixty per cent water. Soil: where plants stand and get their minerals. And the right temperature, roughly zero to forty-five degrees. Now visit the Tsitsikamma forest. Rain every month, deep soil, mild weather. It is packed with trees, ferns and birds. Now the Richtersveld. Same Sun, same air. But almost no rain, thin stony soil and scorching days. A few fat-leaved plants storing water. One missing item from the backpack, water, holds everything back. Scientists call it the limiting factor. Find the missing item and you know why a place looks the way it does.
visual_style: A whiteboard backpack unpacking five icons; a split screen of a dense forest and an empty stony plain, with a big water drop crossed out on the desert side.
mood: Curious comparison with an aha moment.
pacing: Quick backpack unpacking, slow side-by-side comparison, punchy limiting-factor reveal.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find the limiting factor in your own neighbourhood.
